notes: The owner's tests are visible change across the pages, fine line art, glow where the phosphor is, and grounded, cool colour elsewhere. Grid Console Lit Track and Track Diagram Scanlined meet all four best, because they carry the Signal Box tracks and rings the owner called high style and keep real CRT light on tubes and lit marks. Their colour is cool and low-chroma. Desk Terminal Vera Card is the most orderly page but carries fewer fine lines. The Lit Index family has the best typesetting but leans on warm cream, amber and brass, which the owner has repeatedly marked off-motif. It also loses the glow and line language outside Home. Green Desk is bold but runs into the owner's dislike of dominant beige cases and pink and mauve accents.

scores.why: The owner's own complaints: too bright, too contrasty, near-monochrome green. It has the glow, but it is one wash of green. Fine as the yardstick.

The most complete system. It has the line art the owner asked to see echoed (tracks, lamps, a timetable margin on To do, the NOW line, the ring-and-elbow page heads, a lit foot lamp). It has real CRT light (glowing question, bezelled tubes, a gauge, a grid floor), a cool grounded ground with a small section palette, and every page changes, not just the corner.

It carries the Signal Box language the owner praised on Chat, To do, Status and the bar dot. The serif titles, the keycap tray with radio dots and the scanlined bloom on 'mind' are tasteful, and the colour is grounded. Home's first screen is still close to today's, which is the only 'nearly identical' risk.

It has the same strong Grid Console base, and the question typed on the tube under a block cursor is the truest CRT gesture here. But the left box is left bare and dark, and the poster question, the page's strongest statement, is lost.

A coherent, grown-up terminal: Vera card, a per-page tube (chart, gauge, bar readout), tight rows with facts on the right, and a contents plate. The CRT soul and glow are real and the colour is grounded. It is busy and sidebar-heavy, with fewer fine lines, and a long empty left column on Home.

Lit Index plus a brass rail on Chat, which is a line the owner likes. But the giant condensed bone type, amber and orange plates and brass lean warm, which the owner has called off-motif. The CRT lives only on Home and the monitors, and the dimmed scanline MIND reads a little muddy.

A cooler teal ground, a cyan companion and halo on the mark and current tab address the owner's colour and light asks. At card size it is almost indistinguishable from its parent, so it fails the 'reflect more of the page' test. The structure is the same type-heavy index.

Striking typesetting with big condensed titles and a clear page identity, and a very different page from today. The warm cream and amber plates, the near-absence of line art or glow past Home, and generic editorial lists on inner pages cost the CRT feel.

A bold, coherent idea with a lot of period character: scanline title bars, pixel type and a dotted time spine. But the beige putty cases are exactly the dominant monitor-case the owner dislikes, the pink and mauve rails jar, and the pixel face and kitsch make it less a modern app than a costume.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the tracks, lamps, tubes and grid floor, which are the signature. Fix the empty hatched panels beside the three setup cards and the sparse chat page. Make sure the grid floor and glow do not tip into 'Matrix' on pages without a monitor.

Keep the chat track, the status ring-and-elbow head, the keycap tray and the scanlined key word. Give Home's first screen a visible structural change (a tube grid floor or a track from the head), since it is close to today's. Strengthen the scanlines at half size.

Keep the typed question on the tube with its cursor, and the light numerals. Put a short lit line or the Next up summary in the left box, or let the tube sit centred, so the left column is not an empty dark field. Bring back some of the poster scale in the head.

Keep the Vera glass strip with its lamp, the per-page tubes and the tight fact rows. Shorten the empty left column below the terminal on Home. Add a few fine track or ring lines to the lists so it echoes the line art the owner likes.
Keep the rail on Chat and the lit-square checkbox. Swap the brass for a cool steel or a dim green, and cool the amber plates. Bring tracks to To do and Status so the rail is not a one-page idea.

Keep the haloed mark and current tab and the breathing lamp that runs only while she answers. The cyan companion needs to appear on links, selected filters or chart marks to be seen. Make the ground and section colours differ enough from the parent to count.

Keep the giant condensed index head, which is the best typesetting in the field. Replace the warm cream with a cooler or greener bone, add fine tracks or rings to the lists, and restore the glow on lit words, since only Home and the tubes carry light.

Keep the scanline-striped title bars and the NOW spine. Drop the beige case for a thin graphite one, make the rails cyan or dim green instead of pink and mauve, and use the pixel face only for headings.

notes: The eight finalists divide into three. Lit Index (head-2, mut-5, mut-6) wins on the single scanlined, blooming MIND, but its lists and chat are print rather than lit. Grid Console (head-5, mut-11) has the most alive lit track and, with mut-11, the typed tube. Desk Terminal mut-1 puts the most real CRT hardware in the page content: glass question, charted tube and gauge. The edge is small between the top four, and my order puts the richest tube-in-content first. Wild-1 is vivid but is a different retro. Mut-3 is the calmest and loses the soul. Nearly all finalists beat today on grounded colour; the soul question is whether the light is kept where the phosphor is, and mut-1 and mut-5 do that best.

scores.why: The original tube light is all there: halo on the key word, bloom and scanlines on the monitors, glowing dots. But the page around it is one green wash and a lot of it is generic dark cards, so the soul is real and diffuse.

The most green-screen content of the field. The question is typed in VT323 on a glass strip with a block cursor and a breathing Listening lamp. Next up is a bezelled tube with a plotted chart and a grid floor, and Status gets a real gauge monitor. Light stays on glass and lamps, and the rows, filter keys and chat rail change across pages. It is boxy and the left column runs empty.

Brings back the tube's light on the page's biggest word: raster lines through a white-hot-to-phosphor gradient under a bloom. The beige-cased monitors are still real, and the glow is scarce. The brass chat rail ends in a lit ring, and the Send key throws afterglow rings. The whole page is re-typeset as a lit index. The rail leaves the Chat page sparse.

The question typed on the Next up tube under a block cursor with a lamp status line is the purest phosphor idea here, and the lit track and NOW chip carry through every page. The cost is a plain, empty box on Home and a question that is smaller than the poster it replaced, so Home's first glance is weaker.

Same lit-index system as the parent with the kit's two-layer halo put back on the mark and the current page name, which is the owner's ask. The teal-black ground is a small step off black, and the cyan hardly shows. It reads almost the same as its parent, so the gain is real but small.

The scanlined, blooming MIND poster over cream condensed type is the strongest single recovery of tube light, and giant lit-index titles across Ideas, Status and Plans are a change the family sees on every page. Light is concentrated in the poster and the monitor, and the lists and chat are quiet print.

A lit track with glowing node lamps, a NOW chip, a perspective grid floor and an 'UP' lamp gives the page a vector-display aliveness. Many bordered cards and the grid make it busier than the others. The question is a flat bloom with no scanlines or typed feel.

A bold, coherent 1984 system: pixel face, scanline-striped title bars, putty monitors and a dotted time spine. It is alive, but it leans to early Mac and GEM rather than a phosphor tube. The lit green is spread over many windows, and pixel type costs readability.

Scanlined bloom on 'mind', keycap trays with lit radio dots and a calm vertical chat track are tasteful. The cream serif titles and warm neutrals pull the page away from a green-screen feel, and the scanlines are fine enough to read as texture at normal size.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the typed glass strip, the Listening lamp, the charted Next up tube and the gauge monitor. Fix the long empty stretch below the terminal on Home: let the tube end where its content ends, or lift the Contents plate beside it. Reduce the nested card borders.

Keep the scanlined MIND, the rail with its lit ring and the key echo. Tighten the Chat page by narrowing the dead margins beside short lines, and drop the repeated 'What's on your mind' opener. Give lists and rows a little of the same afterglow.

Keep the typed question on the tube. Put something in the left column of Home (the quiet box with chips is too empty), perhaps by making the box taller and lit, and set the question one step larger so it keeps the poster's authority.

Keep the halo on the mark and the page name. Use the cyan companion in more places (numerals, links, the Status head) or drop it. Restore a blacker ground so the green screens still pop out of a true black.
Keep the poster and the index heads. Add one more lit element in the lists, such as a glowing designator or today's row, so the pages below Home are not all unlit print.
Keep the lit track, the NOW chip and the lamp footer. Quiet the grid and the card borders. Give the Home question the scanline bloom or the typed treatment the sibling designs have.

Keep the spine with NOW, the putty monitors and the window title bars. Use the pixel face only for bars and headings, and set body, labels and numerals in a readable face. Make the stripes fainter on dense pages and add a halo on the lit key word.

Keep the keycap tray and the chat track. Swap the cream serif titles for a face with CRT character, or light the title's key glyph. Make the scanlines coarser so they read at the size of the page, and keep the glow on the live things.

notes: The Lit Index line is the strongest typographic statement, and the rail chat in mut-5 is the best conversation. Green Desk is the boldest and most coherent idea, and the family would see it on every page. The Track Diagram with serif titles is the most refined. The Grid Console variants are competent but less personal. Mut-6's teal tint is too subtle to separate it from its parent.

scores.why: The original glow and monitors are the signature, but one green on black with generic cards. It is the Matrix-like page the family described, with little personality in the type.

The Lit Index poster typography (giant condensed titles, mono folios, section-coloured bars, scanlined MIND, brass rail chat) changes every page and has a clear printed-index personality. Light stays on the key word, the mark and the monitors. The rail chat is the loveliest conversation here, though Plans, Status and Settings are plainer than Home.

The most original idea: a 1984 desktop on a green tube, with scanline title bars, putty monitors and a dotted time spine. It is coherent across every page and charming enough that the family would smile. The pixel face and mauve spine risk gimmick and some roughness at nav size, but it is the bravest and still readable.

Fraunces serif titles with typed counts, keycap filters with lit radio dots, a vertical Vera track in chat and a week dial on Plans give a warm, considered editorial feel. The scanlined key word is lit and the grounded companions are tasteful. A little soft and conventional next to the boldest, but very polished.

The question typed on the tube under a block cursor is the closest return of the original CRT effect, and the lit NOW track, gauge and banded rows give a good system. The Home left column is left empty and the poster question is lost, so Home is less memorable.

The Vera card beside a bezelled tube on a grid floor, the dial-pip contents rail and the gauged rows are a distinctive instrument-panel idea that varies every page. It is dense and busy, with an empty stretch on Home, and it is closer to a dashboard than a personality.

Strong typographic identity and the section colour bars give it a real voice. The chat is a plain transcript without the rail's charm, and the MIND is dim and heavy. A good base that its child mut-5 improves on.
The Lit Index with a teal-black ground, cream chalk ink and a lit mark halo. The shift is a modest tint, and at card size it reads almost identical to the parent. The cyan companion barely shows.

A coherent Grid Console with a NOW track, a good Status gauge and a lit footer lamp. The look is competent but familiar cards-and-lines, and it has less of a distinct point of view than the others. Its child mut-11 does more with the glass.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the giant condensed titles, folio bars and rail chat. Fix the sparse space beside short chat lines, brighten the dim MIND toward #6dff9c, and bring the Status, Plans and Settings pages up to the same richness as Home.
Keep the scanline title bars, putty monitors and spine. Rein in the pixel face to headings only, use Atkinson or Plex for body, and fix the uneven pixel icons at nav size.
Keep the Fraunces titles, keycaps and chat track. Strengthen the scanlines so they are visible at card size, and give the lists a little more contrast and weight.
Keep the typed question on the tube and the NOW track. Fill Home's left column with the poster question or Vera's presence, and keep the light numerals from thinning the heads.
Keep the Vera card and tube on the grid floor. Trim the rail's pips, close the empty stretch on Home, and give the title a more characterful face.
Keep the index heads and colour bars. Add the chat rail from mut-5 and lift the dim scanlined MIND.
Keep the lit mark and page-name halo and the breathing lamp. Push the teal and cyan companions so they appear on rules, tabs and figures; a tint alone does not read.
Keep the lit NOW track and gauge. Take the typed glass or a bolder head treatment from its children to give the page more voice.

notes: The two strongest ideas are the Grid Console's lit track (a spine, a NOW node, numbered sections with an icon and a fading rule) and the Lit Index's editorial heads (a giant condensed title, a folio, a coloured section bar), and they would combine well. Both change the content of every page rather than a corner, which is the owner's test. Grid Console brings back the most of the original phosphor light, with a bloom and halo on the live things and a glowing dot at the base, while the Lit Index is calmer and more typographic but keeps its light mostly on the Home headline. The Chat rail in mut-5 is the best conversation treatment. Wild-1 is the most distinct, but its metaphor costs readability and calm. The Chalk Teal ground and mut-3's keycap filters are nice grounded touches.

scores.why: Competent and consistent card system, but nearly monochrome green on near-black. Every page reads as the same rounded dark cards, with little hierarchy beyond size, and the original CRT light is only on the monitors and the key word.

The most complete system on the sheet. A lit spine with a NOW node, numbered sections with an icon, title and fading rule, corner-ticked cards, one section hue per page, condensed headings with a counted figure, and a grid-floor footer. It holds on Status, Plans, To do and Settings with the same grammar, and the halo, bloom and glowing dots return where the phosphor belongs. It is dense, and the card lattice on Settings and Ideas is still fairly busy.

The Lit Index system with an extra layer of care: a brass rail chat thread, lit-square checkboxes, and a key echo. Giant condensed titles, a folio, section bars and ruled lists change every page visibly, and the type hierarchy is the strongest here. The rail leaves Chat sparse and the opener repeats Home's headline, but it is still the best chat in the Lit Index family.

A confident editorial system: massive Archivo condensed titles, mono folios, coloured section bars and hairline rules, with a scanlined bloom on MIND and a bezelled monitor. It is clearly different from today on every page, and the typesetting is a pleasure. Light is concentrated in the Home headline, and the Home title is so large it competes with the form.

Lit Index on a teal-black ground with cream chalk ink and a lit mark and active tab. The ground is more grounded and distinct, but the change from its parent is small on every page, and the cyan companion barely shows.

A different structure: a left terminal column of plates (On this page contents, status foot) beside the content, with a Vera card and a bezelled tube on Home. Clear, calm and useful, with good tabular rows and strong controls. The terminal column leaves long empty stretches on Chat and To do, and the sidebar repeats the nav's job.

Grid Console with the question typed on the tube. It keeps all of head-5's system strengths, and the banded rows and light numerals are fine details. But it removes the poster question from the form, which leaves Home's left column with a plain box and a dead area, and the VT323 question is smaller than the headline it replaces.

A calm, readable Track Diagram with a Fraunces serif title, a recessed keycap tray with radio dots, and a good Chat rail. It has the most grounded feel and the best filters. The serif/sans/mono/pixel mix is less cohesive, the structure is close to today's card layout, and the scanlined key word is hard to see at normal size.

A bold, fully worked idea: striped title bars, a time-ruler spine, putty monitors, one hue per window. It is coherent and clearly different, but the Pixelify headings, the zeros with slashes, and the window chrome on every panel add noise and look dated. The whole system leans on a metaphor more than on usefulness, and the page reads less calm.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit spine, numbered section heads and corner-ticked cards. Quiet the grid floor and the faint hatching on empty card cells, and give Settings and Ideas a list or row variant so not every page is a card lattice.
Keep the rail thread, lit-square checkbox and key echo. Tighten the Chat page so short lines do not float in dead space, and drop the repeated Vera asks opener, or make it the empty state only.

Keep the index heads and section bars. Scale the Home headline down so the box is the first read, and carry some of the halo to the mark, the active tab and the live dots so the light is not only on MIND.
Keep the teal ground, the cream chalk and the lit mark. Use the cyan companion on a real job (links, the count figures, the Plans colour) so the change shows beyond the ground.
Keep the Vera card and the gauged rows. Collapse the terminal column to a slim rail, or make the contents sticky, on pages without much content, and fill the Chat and To do dead space.
Keep the light numerals and the faint row banding. Put the poster question back on the box, or give the tube's typed question more size, and fill the empty left column on Home.

Keep the keycap tray with radio dots, the Chat rail and the grounded palette. Drop the serif title or settle on a single heading face, and make the scanlines on the key word coarser so they show at 100%.

Keep the spine with its NOW tag and the one-hue-per-window idea. Replace Pixelify with a legible face for the body and nav, and cut the title-bar stripes to the primary window so the panels stay calm.

notes: The index-head family (head-2, mut-5, mut-6) is best on this lens. The giant lit question leads straight to the one Send action, the numbered tabs and big section numerals let you find things quickly, and the change shows across every page, not just a corner. The scanlined bloom on the headline also brings back the tube's light where attention belongs. mut-1 is the best structured and easiest to scan in its lists. head-5 and mut-3 have good state signals (NOW track, keycap radios) but a busier Home. mut-11 and wild-1 trade clarity for atmosphere. Today's page is a clear, calm baseline with weak hierarchy beyond the box.

scores.why: Clear but flat: Home gives the composer the most weight, yet the tube competes beside it and all sections read at one level. It has the original glow but little hierarchy beyond the box, and 45 targets are under 44px.

The giant scanlined 'WHAT'S ON YOUR MIND?' leads to a full-width Send key, and the sight line (title, action, content) holds when squinted. Numbered index tabs and big section numerals with counts make it quick to find things across the page. Only 2 targets are under 44px, and the lit headline brings the tube's light back in the right place.

Keeps head-2's strong hierarchy and adds a chat rail with the family on one side and Vera on the other, ending in a lit 'your turn' ring above the composer. That is a clear conversation sight line. The lit-square checkbox states are legible, but the chat is sparser and the opener repeats Home's headline.

Same clear index, hierarchy and large targets as head-2, with the mark and current page name lit so 'where am I' is easier to see. The teal-black and cream shift reads across the page, but contrast is the lowest of the group (4.9) and the cyan barely appears.

The 'On this page' contents plate and tabular rows with right-aligned facts (when, who, number) are quick to scan, and no Home targets are under 44px. The Vera card with its glass question and Listening line is a clear anchor. The phone's composer and Send are smaller, the Ideas filters run tall, and there is less drama in the squint.

The NOW track with due dots on To do is a fast read of what is late, and the bezelled tube plus a lit question is a good Home. The lattice of small cards is busier at a glance, 20 targets are under 44px, and the sight line is less decisive than the index designs.

Keys as a recessed tray of keycaps with radio rings show which filter is in force more clearly than any other design, and the track-diagram chat is readable. The Home headline is smaller and quieter, the track chrome is busy, and the scanlines on 'mind' mostly read as bigger and brighter.

The typed question on the tube is atmospheric, but it moves the headline away from the composer, which becomes a plain unlabeled field, so the page asks less clearly. VT323 wraps and the poster hierarchy is lost. The light numerals are thin, 21 targets are under 44px, and otherwise it matches head-5.

Distinctive and every panel is a window, but the pixel type and striped title bars add noise and hurt legibility on dense pages. The spine and NOW tag help orientation, and the Send key is big. It is the most different from today but the slowest to scan, with 21 targets under 44px.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit headline, full-width Send and numbered index. On the phone, cut the headline height so the composer starts higher, and give the chips and tab bar 44px targets.
Keep the rail, margin times and 'your turn' ring. Drop the 'Vera asks' opener or make it compact, and tighten the short-line gaps. Make the checkbox lit square slightly larger.
Keep the lit mark and page name. Raise body ink contrast above 5 on the teal ground, and bring the cyan into links or filter states so it is visible.
Keep the contents plate, tabular rows and glass status line. Enlarge the phone Send key, replace the tall Ideas filter column with a compact row, and lift the headline weight.
Keep the NOW track and due dots, and thin out the lattice of tiny cards so the page is calmer. Raise the 44px targets and make the headline decisive.
Keep the keycap tray with radio states and use it in other filters. Quiet the track chrome, and make the key word the signature green, bigger, with clear scanlines.
Keep the typed tube as a status display, but restore a labelled headline above the composer so the ask is obvious. Use a bolder face for the numerals and give the plain field a lit border.
Keep the spine with its NOW tag and the window bars on key panels only. Use Pixelify just for titles and nav, set body text in Atkinson, and reduce the striped bars on dense lists.

notes: The two typographic systems that look designed are the condensed Archivo with mono folios and tracked caps (Lit Index and Grid Console) and the Fraunces counted heads (mut-3). The Lit Index family is the clearest on the page: a heavy title, a hairline, a mono folio, quiet Plex facts and condensed list titles. Its three finalists differ little in type, so the tiebreakers are ground cohesion (teal, mut-6), the restraint of the chat (head-2) and the light (mut-6's halo on the mark and current page). Grid Console is close behind and has the best counted figure. The VT323 questions in mut-1 and mut-11 give up the poster's authority. The pixel face in wild-1 fights legibility at small sizes. All of the top five change the type across every page, so they pass the owner's test and are not corner washes.

scores.why: Clean DM Sans-style hierarchy with a competent but flat scale: one bold title weight, muted decks, little tracking or figure work, and no folios or running heads.

The full Lit Index type system: heavy condensed Archivo titles, tracked mono folios and nav, Plex body and tabular facts, now on a calmer cream-on-teal ground. The kit's halo on the mark and the current page's name puts some tube light back. The change shows on every page and the scale is coherent.

The same Lit Index typesetting: a giant condensed title over a hairline with a coloured stub, a mono folio, small tracked-cap labels, and condensed Ideas row titles beside quiet mono facts. The scanlined MIND is a strong poster word, though it is large enough to border on glare. The olive-black cream is a touch less cohesive than the teal version.

A very good hierarchy: condensed titles with a counted figure (Ideas 12, underlined, with a tracked 'IN ALL') and mono folios. The Home question is a contained poster in the box rather than a page-wide shout. Body sizes are a little small, and it is more decorated by grid and lines than the Lit Index.

Typographically the same as head-2 on Home and Ideas. The Chat rail with margin timestamps and the repeated 'Vera asks' opener adds clutter and leaves sparse short lines, so it is slightly less tidy than head-2's ruled log.

Fraunces titles with a counted figure in the Ideas and Status heads are warm and refined and clearly different from today's. The serif, DM Sans body and VT323 glass make three voices, but the serif sits well against the phosphor mono. Layout stays close to today's, so there is less typographic structure across the lists.

The best list typesetting on the cards: column heads (DRIVE, FOR, #), right-aligned tabular facts and neat 'On this page' contents. The Home question in VT323 is small and the card is crowded with many small labels, so the hierarchy is flatter.

The Grid Console type system is intact, but setting the question in small wrapping VT323 loses the strongest statement on Home. The loose apostrophe is a flaw, and 300-weight numerals at wdth 62 look thin against the heavy titles.

Pixelify Sans titles with Atkinson labels give a strong identity, but the pixel face costs refinement at small sizes. The stripe title bars, extra empty bars and uneven pixel icons make the page noisier, and the hierarchy is flatter than the condensed systems.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the teal ground, the cream chalk ink and the halo on the mark. Cap the MIND poster a size smaller so it glows without glare, and give the cyan companion a real job such as figures or links.
Keep the condensed title with hairline and folio. Reduce the headline scale about 15% and tighten the gap between the title and the deck on wide screens. Move the ground toward the teal of mut-6.
Keep the counted figure head with the underlined number and tracked unit. Raise the small mono labels about 1px for legibility and take the Lit Index's looser leading in the card rows.

Keep the lit-square checkboxes and the key echo. Drop the repeated 'Vera asks' opener, and bring the Chat back toward head-2's ruled log with margin times only, since the bubbles on the rail leave short lines stranded.

Keep Fraunces for page titles and the counted figure. Apply the same serif and figure treatment to the section heads and list rows so it is a system rather than a head-only change. Use old-style or tabular figures consistently in the lists.
Lift the tabular column-head row treatment into every list. Set the Home question in a larger face than 28px VT323 and cut the number of tiny labels in the Vera card.
Return the question to the condensed poster and keep the typed cursor only as a small status line. Raise the numeral weight to 400 to match the titles, and fix the apostrophe spacing.
Limit Pixelify Sans to the titles, the NOW tag and the buttons, and set the body, nav and labels in Atkinson. Remove the empty striped bars over the section heads, which carry no text.

notes: The leaders are the designs that make the next step and the state of things plain. mut-1 puts the whole conversation in one card, shows overdue in words, and spends no 44px targets on Home. mut-3 is the quiet, legible alternative with a clear filter tray. The Lit Index family looks the most different from today and has real hierarchy, but on the phone the headline pushes the box down and the controls are underline-only, so it falls to the middle and bottom. The Grid and Green Desk families have many targets under 44px and add decoration that competes with the content. Today's page scores 6: it is plain and readable but gives no cue for what is late or where you are.

scores.why: Plain and readable, and the phone's Home puts the box first. But a task that is overdue looks the same as one that is not, the sizes are small, and nothing says where you are beyond a faint pill.

Best walk-through. On the phone, Vera's question, status line, box, From select, mic, Send and chips are one card, so the first screen answers where to start. To do shows 'was due 6 days ago' in amber and has an obvious 'Add a task' key. Filters are explicit buttons, the tube counts Late and This week, and a side index with a 'Ready' status line tells you the state of things. 0 targets under 44px on Home. The cost is a long empty left column and small row text on desktop.

Calm, legible DM Sans and serif hierarchy, and 1 target under 44px. The Show filters are a recessed tray of keys with a lit radio ring, so the current state is visible. Phone Home has the box and Send above the fold. To do has a due timeline with a NOW marker. The scanlined 'mind' is decoration that costs nothing. Change from today is moderate and mostly in the type.

Phone Home is good: box, Send and chips come before the tube. To do reads as a dated timeline with a lit NOW node, and Settings cards each say how they stand. The weak points are 20 targets under 44px, a lot of grid and rule noise that competes with the content, and a ragged layout with all the little tags and 'UP' lamps.

Controls are the clearest in the field: sunken fields, a real caret on selects, a big Send key, and a solidly filled active tab in the section colour. The change reaches every page, which is what the owner asked for. But the striped title bar on every panel is decoration and visual noise, Pixelify at small sizes is harder to read, the dotted spine uses margin, and 21 Home targets are under 44px. The mic placement under the Title field is odd.

Huge condensed titles give an unmistakable hierarchy and Send is a full-width key. But on the phone the 'WHAT'S ON YOUR MIND?' headline takes most of the first screen. The mono nav and labels are tiny, selects and fields are underline-only so they barely look like controls, and To do does not show overdue. Settings is a clean list.

Same grid console as head-5, but the question is moved onto the tube and the box is pushed below it, so Send is further from the top. The box is then a plain field, so the greeting and the action are less tied together. Banded rows and light numerals help scanning, but the thin Archivo 300 numerals lose weight at a glance. It has 21 small targets.

Lit Index with a warmer cream ink, teal-black ground and a lit mark and current page name. This helps a little with the current-page cue and the ground reads calmer. But it inherits the Lit Index problems (the headline fills the phone's first screen, tiny mono nav, underline selects, no overdue cue). Minimum text contrast is down to 4.9 and the cyan barely shows.

Lit Index plus a rail chat, a Send key with echo rings and lit-square checkboxes. The empty frame with a small lit square is a less conventional tick than a check mark, so it is a weaker state cue. The key echo is a distraction. The rail thread leaves a lot of empty space. Otherwise identical to head-2 and no easier to use.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the Vera card, the amber 'was due N days ago' rows, the Add key and the Ready foot line. Fix the empty left column on Home by moving the Contents plate beside or below the tube, and stretch the row text a size up on desktop.
Keep the keys tray with its radio ring and the timeline. Make the overdue dates read as 'was due N days ago' as mut-1 does, and widen the Add something row into a clear primary key.

Keep the dated To do timeline and the Home order (box before tube). Raise the 20 small targets (nav chips, tags) to 44px, and thin out the grid and rule lines on Status so the lamps and cards carry the state.

Keep the filled section-coloured active tab and the sunken fields. Drop the stripes from the small title bars (or keep them only on the lit window), move the mic back beside its field, and set Pixelify only on titles, not at small sizes.
Cap the Home headline to about two lines so the box sits above the fold, give selects a full border and caret, bring the nav mono up a size, and show overdue on tasks.
Put the box above the tube again or give the typed question a visible caret into the box. Keep the row banding but put the numerals back at regular weight.
Keep the lit mark and current page name. Move the chalk ink and the cyan into the controls (focus, selected filters) so the colour has a job, and fix the Lit Index issues listed under head-2.
Use a standard tick inside the lit frame for checkboxes so the checked state is clear. Keep the rail but pull the thread closer to the margin, and limit the echo to the primary Send key.

notes: The owner's test is a change across the page content, and mut-1, mut-3 and head-2 all pass it with different bets. Mut-1 is the most grounded and usable, with materials in solid things, readable rows and one rail system. Mut-3 is the warmest, and its serif and lit track give a personality that does not read as a costume. Head-2 has the best type and the best revival of the original tube's light, but its poster scale is a legibility and glare risk. Mut-5 and mut-6 are near-duplicates of head-2, and mut-11 is a near-duplicate of head-5 that regresses Home. The grid floor in head-5 moves toward Matrix and Tron. Wild-1 is coherent but a costume.

scores.why: Calm and legible, but it is the Matrix-ish monochrome green the owner called too bright. Same card rhythm on every page, and neutral type with no hierarchy beyond the glow.

A change across every page, not a corner: the Vera card with its lit glass strip, tight rows with right-hand facts, a bezelled tube and 'on this page' rail on each page, and amber only on late. Grounded, readable and the most system-like. Weaknesses: the rail and 'Ready' strip repeat on every page, the Ideas kind filter is a clumsy button grid, and the Home left column is slightly spare.

The serif titles with counts, the track and NOW light, the keycap filter tray and the haloed question give warmth and a personality that is not a costume. It keeps real bloom where attention goes and is calmer than the grid. Weaknesses: the Ideas tray is heavy with radio dots, Fraunces plus Plex plus VT323 is a lot of faces, and the scanlines on 'mind' are barely visible.

The boldest typographic change on every page (giant condensed titles, folios, coloured section bars, hatched kind swatches) and the scanlined bloom 'MIND' is the best original-phosphor revival. Weaknesses: the 80px poster titles shout and the nav and facts drop to roughly 8-9px. Status and Settings are sparse, and the cream-on-black is high-contrast again.

Rich lit-track structure with NOW, late dots and a footer lamp, a real Status dial, and bloom around the box. It is clearly different from today on every page. Weaknesses: the perspective grid floor and green glow veer toward Tron or Matrix, the card density is high, and green still dominates the colour.

Head-2 plus a brass rail on Chat. The Chat page is a visible change with good margin timestamps, but everything else is identical to head-2. The rail leaves a sparse, tall Chat, and the checkbox and key-echo changes are invisible on the cards.
Head-2 on a teal-black ground with cream chalk. It is nearly a duplicate; the cyan companion barely appears, and the teal-green ground reads as a tinted wash. The mark halo is a small gain.

Coherent and distinctive (title bars, spine, putty monitors), and it keeps full tube light. But it is a 1984 costume. Pixel type on every heading hurts legibility, the stripe bars clutter every panel, and the pixel zeros in '$0.00' and times read oddly. It is the least calm of the field.

Head-5 with a typed question on the tube. Home's box loses its own question and becomes a bare field with a dead dark area below it, which is worse than head-5's poster. Elsewhere it is identical to head-5, so it is a near-duplicate with a Home regression. Banded rows and light numerals are barely visible.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the Vera card, tight rows with right-hand facts and the per-page tube. Drop the repeated Ready strip. Make the Ideas kind filter a select or a compact pill row. Fill the Home left column below the card so it does not end short.

Keep the serif and count head, the lit track and the haloed question. Make the scanlines on 'mind' coarser so they show. Make the filter tray lighter, with the radio dot only on the active key. Settle on two text faces.

Keep the folio and section-bar system, the scanlined MIND and the hatch swatches. Cap titles near 64px, raise the nav and fact text to at least 11px, and add rows or tiles to Status and Settings so they are less empty.
Keep the lit track, the NOW and late dots, the dial and the UP lamp. Fade the grid floor to a corner or the footer only. Add one grounded companion to the cards so green is not the whole palette.
Keep the Chat rail with its margin times and the lit 'your turn' ring. Tighten the rail's gutters so Chat is not tall and sparse. Fold it into head-2 rather than shipping it as a separate design.
Keep the haloed mark and current-page name and the breathing lamp. Use the cyan on links and the Plans accent so it shows. Keep the ground neutral black, not teal-green.

Keep the spine with the lit NOW and the hue-per-window idea. Use Pixelify only for the logo and the page title, and put titles and bars in a readable sans. Drop the stripe fill on the quiet panels. Fix the zero glyphs.

Put the typed question and its lit key word back on the box side, or keep the poster question. Use the tube for Next up only. Keep the light-weight numerals and the banded rows, which are the useful parts.

notes: The field splits into three families. The Track Diagram family (head-1, mut-3, mut-4) is the closest to what the owner called high style: thin tracks, rings and lamps that carry through Home, Chat, Ideas and To do, with grounded amber, violet and cyan companions and the key word and monitors still lit. The Grid Console family (head-4, head-5, mut-9 to 12) adds the grid floor and haloed cards, and head-5 has the most complete lamp-and-track language. Lit Index and Blueprint are the boldest page-wide changes, so they cannot be called near identical, but the poster MIND is close to glare and the blueprint's cream and grid sit off-period. Many of this round's mutants change little at card size (mut-2, mut-6, mut-8), which is the owner's standing complaint. The best new phosphor idea is mut-11's typed question on the tube, and the weakest on the CRT soul is the Green Desk. Today's page scores low because it has no line language and its colour is one wash.

scores.why: Today's page is the lit tube but near monochrome green, with no line language and boxes in a single wash, which is what the owner asked to move away from.
Graphite terminal, gauged rows and a NOW rail make Home visibly different, but the tall left column and plain tabular lists drift toward generic modern dark.

The nearest heir to Signal Box, the owner's favourite: a ringed head, a chat thread hanging from Vera's mark, a lamped To do track and a Coming up track, with the lit key word, serif titles and amber/violet/cyan pencils all grounded, on every page.

The boldest typesetting by far, a giant condensed Archivo head with a scanlined phosphor MIND, section-coloured bars and hatched kind swatches; it changes every page but its lines are plain rules, not tracks, and the huge green word risks the glare the owner disliked.
A teal blueprint with a grid, title blocks and section pencils is a real whole-page change with a fine line language, but cream and scalloped bubbles lean off-period for a CRT and the grid is busy.

Perspective-grid floor, a lit rail with NOW pills, cornered cards and a haloed Vera card keep the tube's light where the phosphor is, with amber, violet and cyan companions; the serif/mono mix is handsome, though some cards are boxy.

The same grid console with condensed bold headers, folio numbers and a lamped due-time To do track, the most complete line-and-lamp language of the Grid family, with good glow and clearly grounded colour.
A reference bar: a calm graphite terminal with a lit tube and tidy rows, but it is plain next to the track and grid designs and only a little different from today across pages.

Splitting Home into a Vera card and a bezelled tube on a grid floor with a typed VT323 question is a lovely phosphor moment, but it leaves a long empty column and the rest of the page is the parent's.
A vent row and a bezel groove on the parent's case and a scanlined key word are subtle at card size, so it reads nearly identical to its parent, the owner's exact complaint.

Track Diagram plus a convincingly tube-drawn scanlined bloom on the key word and keycap filters with lit radio dots, so the CRT light returns where attention belongs while the track lines and grounded colour carry through all pages.
The Track Diagram with a giant condensed bone title and a cooler ground adds a real typographic hierarchy on Chat and Ideas, but Home is unchanged and the fifth face adds weight.
Lit Index with a brass rail chat thread and echoing Send rings is a good echo of the owner's line art, but the Home and Ideas are the parent's loud poster and the chat gets sparse.
A teal-black ground, chalk ink and a haloed mark change the whole page's temperature in a grounded way, but the cyan barely shows and it is otherwise the parent.
The blueprint's NOW gauge tick with a scale is a nice lit signal and pencils close the boxes, yet it shares the blueprint's off-period cream and grid busyness.
Chalk ink, mono right-hung facts and seven-day sparklines add detail, but the traces are mostly one spike and it is a quiet difference from the parent.
A counted serif head, a lit rail ending in a 'your turn' Vera card and right-aligned tabular rows make a calmer, more readable page, but they trade away the card variety and some phosphor character.
A giant cream condensed folio title over a mono running head is distinct typesetting with a cooler slate ground, though the lede sits far from the title.
Moving the question onto the tube as typed VT323 under a block cursor is the best phosphor idea in the field, but it leaves the left box bare and the question smaller.

A serif head with a big counted mono figure, the ways to start as a column of keys beside the box and a deeper vented bezel put real new structure on Home and Ideas, though the serif is less of a fit with the Grid voice.

A 1984 desktop with scanline title bars and a dotted ruler spine is the most original and playful take, but the pixel face, putty monitors and mauve spine pull away from the CRT soul and from the owner's dislike of heavy cases.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the scanlined key word and the track language, but let the bloom be visible at half scale by making the scan period coarser, and keep the keycap radio dots only on the one filter in force so Ideas is less busy.

Keep the thread, tracks and lamps on every page; add the tube-drawn bloom on the key word and bring the Plans and Coming up strips to the quality of the To do track so Home's lower half is as strong as its top.

Keep the condensed headers with folio numbers and the lamped To do track, and make the poster question calmer (a little less white) so the grid floor and the card edges carry the glow, not every heading.
Keep the lit rail with NOW pills and the haloed Vera card; thin the card outlines and use the amber, violet and cyan only on kind labels so the boxes feel less boxy.
Keep the typed question and block cursor on the tube, but fill the left column with the Vera greeting and a taller composer so it is not empty, and keep the question size above 1.4rem.

Keep the condensed head type and the hatched swatches, but drop the poster MIND to about 60 percent of its size and dim its bloom, and replace the plain section rules with the owner's tracks and rings.
Keep the Vera card and the typed question beside a bezelled tube; fill the empty column below by moving the Contents and Coming up there.
Keep the scanline-striped title bars as a rule idea, but swap the pixel face for the mono and plain faces, and make the case thin and graphite, not putty.

notes: The phosphor soul is strongest where the question is typed on glass (VT323, block cursor, lit status lamp, chart on the tube) or where one word is drawn as a tube draws it, with raster lines and a layered bloom. Desk Terminal's children (mut-1, mut-2) and Lit Index's giant lit word best recover the original's light and keep the calmer ground. Wild-1 is the most alive new idea, and it changes every page through its lit spine and striped bars, though it drifts toward a Mac desktop. The Track Diagram, Blueprint and Grid Console serif and condensed heads are handsome typesetting and a calmer page, but the glow in them stays on the mark and the monitor, and the pages beyond Home look little lit.

scores.why: Keeps the real tube and halo, but the page around the monitor is a dim, uniform dark card layout, so the light is present without much life.

The Home panel is one graphite terminal with a typed VT323 question, block cursor, lit NEXT UP tag and a chart on the glass; the Status gauge and numbered radar scatter make the tube carry real content.
Calm bone serif titles, a violet count and a ring-and-elbow head are tasteful, but the page is mostly cool and quiet and the glow stays on the mark, the key word and the monitor.
The giant scanlined, blooming MIND over a bone headline is the strongest lit moment in the field and runs across the pages, with a putty-cased monitor; the lit word is almost too large.
The blueprint sheet is a bold page-wide idea with a glowing MIND, but the grid and pencil rules read as drafting more than phosphor, and only the monitor keeps the tube feel.
Grid console with cream serif titles and a bezelled tube beside a lit-edge card is coherent and calm, with little CRT light outside the tube.
The condensed poster headline with a lit MIND, mono folios and a lit track bring more presence than head-4, while the tube sits on a perspective grid floor.
The original terminal idea works: the whole Vera panel and question are typed on the glass with a cursor and the gauge is a real instrument, but it has fewer refinements than its descendants.
Splits Home into a Vera card with a typed VT323 question, a lit LISTENING strip and a tube charting the week on a grid floor; it is the best mix of real tube, lit words and page-wide change.
The scanned, bloomed key word inside a bezelled case with vent slots makes the monitor itself feel like hardware, keeping the terminal's strengths; the raster on 'mind' is subtle.
A scanlined, haloed 'mind' and keycap filters with lit radio dots add some life to the calm Track Diagram, but the rest of the page stays quiet.
The giant condensed index head is a strong typographic change with little added light, and the cooler ground is nearly invisible.
It keeps Lit Index's huge scanlined MIND and adds a brass rail and echoing key press; the lit words and mono labels have real phosphor character.
Lit Index on a teal-black ground with a haloed mark and a breathing lamp is the cleanest version of the glowing headline, though the change is subtle.
The blueprint with a tube-style MIND and a NOW tick keeps glow scarce and meaningful, but it is more drafting table than green screen.
Chalk traces and right-set mono facts are good typesetting and the sparklines add life, but the effect is tonal and the CRT feeling is thin.
Serif folio heads and tight tabular rows are good typesetting on a calm page; it has little added light, and the 20% extra Chat wording adds noise.
The giant condensed title with a mono running head reads like a printed index, and the warmer cream suits the tube, but the page has no new light.
Puts the question on the tube in VT323 with a block cursor and lamp status line, which is the most CRT-faithful idea in the Grid line; it leaves a plain box beside a good tube.
A deeper bezel recess and vent slots make the monitor more physical, and the serif counted head is handsome, but the lit MIND is cropped and little else is new.

A 1984-desktop reading, with scanline title bars, a putty Mac-style tube, a dotted NOW spine lit green and Pixelify type, changes every page and feels alive; the pixel font drifts from green-screen to Mac.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the typed question, the LISTENING strip and the tube's chart on the grid floor. Fill the empty column under the terminal, and keep the question at its full size so the card and the tube do not both go quiet.
Keep the vented bezel and the scanned key word. Make the raster lines coarser so they show at half size, and let the word's face end in the true #6dff9c.
Keep the lit NOW spine and the scanline title bars. Swap Pixelify for a mono face closer to VT323 on page titles, so it reads as phosphor and not as System 1, and keep the glow to the lit windows.
Keep the big scanlined bloom, but limit it to Home's one word and shrink it a size so it frames the page instead of crowding the box. Bring the bone case colour into the other monitors.
Putting the question on the tube is right. Fill the plain box on its left, and set the VT323 question large enough that it does not wrap and loose-set the apostrophe.
Keep the haloed mark and current-page name. Add a faint halo on one more live item per page (the NOW line or the active tab) so the cyan and halo work shows.

notes: The Lit Index and Blueprint families are the only ones that change the page itself rather than its chrome: the first is a poster in condensed type with scanlined light, the second a drafting sheet with pencil colours. The Grid Console and Track Diagram families are competent and consistent, but each page is still mostly rounded cards under a new heading style. The Desk Terminal variants have lovely tube craft in one column and little else. Green Desk is the one entry with a design language of its own (a 1984 desktop on a phosphor tube), and it will not blur into the others. The light has come back on the key word and the NOW marker in a few entrants, mut-7 most convincingly, and it shows only where attention belongs. I would send the Lit Index poster, the Blueprint sheet and the Green Desk wild card to the final, and develop the NOW scale and the Vera card.

scores.why: A good tube and the right green, but the page is still the rounded dark-card stock dashboard with one glowing corner and little typographic personality.
Graphite desk with a bezelled tube and gauged rows is tidy and material, but it reads as a competent dashboard rather than a point of view.
A serif title with counted figure and a lit rail through chat gives a real editorial voice, though Home is still mostly cards.

Giant condensed type with a scanlined, bloomed MIND, hatched swatches and section-coloured bars gives an unmistakable poster-like identity visible on every page, and the CRT light is back where it belongs.
The drafting-sheet idea (grid, rulers, title block, scalloped bubbles, pencil-colour sections) is original and cohesive, with cream and teal as a grounded companion to the green.
Grid console with serif headings and a light trail is polished, but the many boxed cells make it feel like a well-made generic dark UI.
Condensed headings, numbered folios, a perspective grid floor and a lit UP lamp at the foot add real machine character, though Home is busy.
Early desk terminal with the typed question on the glass has charm, but the rest is plain cards and lists.
The Vera card with a typed question on a tube standing on a grid floor is a lovely Home moment, but the rest of the page and the empty left column stay conventional.
Vents and a bezel groove on the case are nice craft but sit in one column, so the page barely changes.
Scanlined key word and keycap filter tray add tube and hardware character on top of a good serif and rail system.
The folio head, a huge bone-white condensed title over serif body on a cooler ground, is a strong typographic upgrade across every page.
Takes the Lit Index poster and adds a brass rail through Chat with ring nodes and margin times, so the conversation has its own memorable character.
Same bold Lit Index with a cooler teal ground and cream chalk, but at card size it is nearly identical to the parent and the cyan barely shows.
Blueprint plus a lit NOW tick running into a graduated scale and a scanlined key word, which is a lovely tie between the drafting idea and the CRT light.
Chalk-tuned blueprint with right-hung tabular facts and seven-day sparklines adds genuine data character, though the traces are sparse in the demo.
A serif folio head and a Your turn Vera card at the end of a lit rail add warmth and editorial feel, but the lattice around it is unchanged.
A giant cream condensed title over a running head on a cooler slate ground changes the feel of every page, though the cards beneath remain generic.
The typed VT323 question with a block cursor on the tube is charming and on-theme, but it costs the poster statement and leaves the left column empty.
Serif masthead with counted figure and raised-key column is pleasant, but the serif is a trope that has faded before and the idea is a small step from its parent.
A 1984 desktop with striped title bars, putty monitors and a dotted time-ruler spine is the boldest and most playful identity here, if a little gimmicky and heavy on window chrome.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the giant condensed titles, the scanlined bloomed MIND and the hatched kind swatches. Tame the Home hero a notch so MIND is not a wall of green, and bring the chat and list bodies up to the title's level of craft.
Keep the NOW tick on its graduated scale and the scanlined key word. Put a real hour in the chip when the data allows, and give the tick scale a gentle afterglow so the one lit line carries the page.
Keep the brass rail and ring nodes. Tighten the empty space either side of short chat lines, and let the Send key echo show on a longer, more visible fade.
Keep the sheet frame, pencil rules and title block. Reduce the grid-mark clutter at the page edges so the sheet reads quieter.

Keep the dotted time-ruler spine, the putty monitors and the Pixelify bars. Drop the striped bar from low-value sections so only the lit windows carry it, and reconcile the pixel icons with the Lucide set.
Keep the Vera card with its typed question and the grid-floor tube. Close the empty left column by letting the Contents plate become a slim rail or move beside the tube.
The chalk-teal ground is good, but make the cyan companion actually visible (links, the ruled sections, the focus ring) so it differs from the parent at a glance.
Keep the folio head with its bone-white condensed title, but drop the fifth face by using the Plex or Fraunces already in use.

notes: The Lit Index family (head-2, mut-5, mut-6) is the strongest on use. The poster headline gives a glance a clear order of title, then the one full-width action, then content. Its mono caps tabs and nav hold as one system, and only 2 of 62 Home targets are small. It also brings back the original tube's layered halo where attention belongs, which the owner asked for. Mut-6 adds the most colour variation (cream chalk and teal) without neon, and mut-5 has the best controls. Blueprint is a calmer, tidier composer, but 17 small targets cost it. Grid Console and Track Diagram mostly stay close to today's page on Home, so a family would see little change; the owner's 'nearly identical' complaint applies to them. Mut-4 and mut-11 weaken the title, so they score lower. Green Desk is the one new idea worth carrying forward: a whole-page window metaphor with a time spine. It needs legibility and target fixes. The Vera card in mut-1 is the clearest first-time grouping.

scores.why: A coherent but uniformly green-lit page: boxed Vera card and a small question, every control glowing the same, the hierarchy flat, with 45 of 57 Home targets under 44px.
The tube leads Home, so the eye goes tube, then box, and every target is 44px or larger, but the question is small and pixel-set and the action sits a screen below it.
An early reference with the question folded into the tube and a plain box below; the structure works but the page shows little variation or new type.

The Vera card puts the question, a Listening status and the box in one clear block, and its 1 under-44 target is the best in the field, but the Next up title wraps to three lines and the look is close to today's.

A poster headline with a layered halo, then a full-width SEND, then the content gives a clean title, action, content order. The mono caps nav and tabs are a consistent system, and only 2 of 62 targets are under 44px; the cost is that the poster pushes Next up below the fold.

The cream headline with a lit key word sits over a single composer panel (From row, Send in the field row), and numbered selects and dashed ways-to-start hold as a system, but 17 Home targets are under 44px.
A coherent grid-and-bezel system, but the question is modest, the Send key stands alone and 20 targets are small, so it reads as a tidier version of today's page.
The heavy condensed question restores the title, then box, then tube order and the tube's chin adds material, but the Home targets are small (20 under 44px).

One Vera card holds the greeting, the typed question, a lit Listening strip and the box, with the Next up tube beside it; the grouping suits a first-time user and all 62 targets pass, but the left column runs empty below it.
The scanlined bloom on 'mind' brings the original tube light back at the one place attention belongs, but the rest is the parent's page, so the difference stays in one spot.
The scanlined key word and a recessed tray of raised filter keys improve the controls, but the tube title wraps and the page is still the Track Diagram.
The question is shrunk to 19px and the cooler ground is nearly invisible, so the hierarchy is weaker than its parent's and the index head only shows on inner pages.

It keeps the Lit Index hierarchy and adds a lit-square checkbox and an echoing Send key, controls with a clear on and off state and a visible press; the chat rail is a sound idea but not visible on this card.

The Lit Index on a teal-black ground with cream ink gives real colour variation (hue entropy 0.66, the highest), the mark and current page are lit, and it keeps the strong hierarchy; the cyan companion barely appears.
The Blueprint composer with a scanlined key word and a lit NOW tick is calm and systematic, with light only where attention goes; the 17 small targets still hold it back.
Chalk colour, right-set mono facts and sparklines are good detail, but at phone size it looks the same as the parent and the sparklines depend on the data.
Rows with right-aligned tabular facts help a list, but Home matches the parent and only five lists are converted, so the system is uneven.
A giant condensed title with a running head makes a good inner-page head, and the blue-slate ground varies the colour, but Home looks unchanged and the lede sits far from the title.
Moving the question onto the tube in small VT323 gives up the poster, the strongest title on Home, and leaves a plain, emptier box.
A serif count head with a column of raised keys beside the box is a neat idea on wide screens, but nothing changes on a phone and the ways to start still sit under the box.

The Green Desk is a complete system: window title bars, a dotted time spine, sunken fields and a full-width Send. It is the most distinct design and avoids the Matrix look, but pixel type and 21 small targets cost legibility and the windows spend phone space.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the teal ground, cream ink and lit mark. Use the cyan companion on more working things (links, the active tab, Status), and let the poster headline give back some height so Next up shows on the first phone screen.
Keep the lit-square checkbox and the Send key's echo, which are the best controls in the field. Trim the chat rail's empty margins and drop the extra 'Vera asks' opener.
Keep the poster headline, full-width SEND and mono caps tabs. Shorten the poster by about 20 percent so the question, the box and the first Coming up row all fit on one phone screen.
Keep the composer panel, numbered select menu and cream headline. Raise the 17 sub-44px Home targets (list rows, ways to start) to 44px.
Keep the window title-bar system and the dotted time spine. Set body copy in Atkinson, not pixel type, raise the small targets to 44px, and make the spine lighter on a phone.
Keep the Vera card with its Listening strip and all targets passing. Shrink the tube to its content and fill the empty left column below the card with Coming up.
Keep the NOW tick with the scale and the single scanlined key word. Show an actual hour beside NOW, and bring the 17 small targets up to 44px.

Put the scanlined bloom on the key word in a lit-poster headline, with the wider pass of the word's gradient kept at #6dff9c, so the original tube light shows across the page and not only in one word.

notes: Most of the field is two lineages in new hats: a Grid Console family (head-4, head-5 and mut-9 to mut-12) and a Track/Lit-Index/Blueprint family. Many of the mutants (mut-2, mut-3, mut-5 through mut-8) are near-duplicates of their parents on the list pages, because their changes are in the chat, a key word's scanlines, or a nav tint that do not show on the cards. By the owner's test those score low. The strongest designs change the head, the type and the row structure on every page. I rate the Grid family highest: it keeps the phosphor light (gauge, lit trail, NOW node) while the colours stay grounded in teal, cream and peach. The condensed giant titles (head-5, mut-10, head-2) give the clearest typographic step. Blueprint is distinct but a costume, and Green Desk is the only genuinely new language, worth developing if its glare is tamed.

scores.why: Yardstick: near-monochrome green with thin cards, flat hierarchy and the Matrix risk; tasteful but little variation or typesetting.
Slate case, gauge and gauged rows are real structure, but the ground goes grey-blue, the nav stays flat and Settings/To do read as plain lists.
Early Desk Terminal: a tidy split but a greyer, duller page with a bare nav and little typographic life; the bar everything else beat.
Serif titles with typed counts, a lit track on Status, a clock dial on Plans and keyed filters are felt on every page; the teal-cream ground is grounded and the green is kept for lamps.

Giant condensed titles, folio numbers and section-coloured hairlines change every page boldly; the glass keeps its bloom. The olive ground is slightly murky and the heavy green bars near the title are a little loud.

A full blueprint sheet with cyan pencils, grid and sheet cartouche is utterly different, but it is a costume (CAD or editor theme), the green share drops to 32%, and the grid is busy under dense text.

A lit trail down the left, serif title with count, tile cards with corner ticks, a NOW chip and a footer lamp give it structure and light together; the grid floor and the many corner ticks are slightly fussy.
Head-4 with the heavy condensed title, numbered nav and the due-date track on To do: the strongest hierarchy and a real phosphor presence (gauge, lit rail, NOW node) without glare.
Only Home changes (a Vera card, a tube beside it); the list pages are the parent's, so the difference the family sees is confined to one page.
A scanlined key word and a vent row on the case are invisible at normal size; effectively a near-duplicate of its parent.
Head-1 with a scanlined word and keycap filters; a pleasant refinement but nearly identical to its parent on the pages shown.
Cream giant serif titles over a hairline are a visible typographic step on every page; the added Archivo face and cooler ground muddy the pairing a little.
Lit Index plus a chat rail, lit-square checkboxes and key echo; the list pages are identical to the parent, so the new work sits in the chat, which these cards do not show.
Lit Index on a teal ground in cream with a cyan companion; on the cards it is almost the parent, and the cyan barely shows.
Blueprint with a scanlined word and a NOW tick on Home; the list pages are unchanged from the parent, and the costume problem remains.
Blueprint in chalk, with tighter rows, a tabular facts column and a sparkline; slightly better typesetting, but still the same blueprint costume and mostly unchanged at a glance.

Tight rows with right-aligned tabular facts and a serif folio are good typesetting and read like a ledger; but the Settings and Status lists were not converted, which makes it inconsistent, and the serif and rail feel thinner than head-5.

Giant cream condensed title over a mono running head, a cooler slate ground and peach type: the clearest page-level typographic change in the Grid family; the title is large enough to crowd the lede on Settings and To do.
Head-5 with light numerals and banded rows; the banding and the thinner figures are subtle, and the real change (a typed question on the tube) is on Home only.
Serif masthead with a big mono count and a deeper bezel; the serif softens the Grid voice, and it repeats a head style that has faded before.
A pixel-font desktop with scanline title bars is a bold, coherent system and the only truly new idea; it risks reading as a costume, and the solid bright-green tab pill is glare.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the condensed title, the numbered nav, the due-date track with a NOW node, and the gauge. Cut the many corner ticks, and make the Status headline and its deck sit on a single baseline rather than floating.

Keep the running head, the cooler slate ground and the cream/peach type. Cap the title near 64px and keep the deck under the title when the page is not wide, so Settings and To do do not strand the lede.

Keep the folio index head, the large settings names with D1..D9 numerals, and the hairlines. Warm the olive ground a step toward the teal family and shorten the bright-green end bars so they stay accents.
Keep the lit trail, the NOW chip and the footer lamp. Drop the grid-floor perspective at the foot and the extra corner ticks; the serif title wants a heavier weight beside the condensed variants.

Keep the scanline title bars, the time-ruler spine and the one-hue-per-window rule. Tone the active tab from a solid bright fill to a lit outline, and soften the pixel face to headings only so body text keeps its calm.
Keep the tight ledger rows with right-aligned tabular facts; carry them to Settings, Status and Plans lists as well so the rule holds on every page.
Keep the clock dial and the serif title with its typed count; the Status track is good. Lift the keycap filters from mut-3 into it.
